items.e: In the name of God who commandsthat a fire offering be brought before him.I begin to explain the book And The Lord Called Unto Moses . AND THE LORD CALLED. We find two reasons for the covenant made with an individual. It is also possible for one commandment to have many reasons. The commandment regarding the burnt offering and the sacrifice are examples of the latter, for when the officiant offers each part in its proper time, then the part which has a part in the world to come is saved. Therefore the meaning of le-khapper (to make atonement) (v. 4) is to give ransom. The opening of the Torah portion Ki Tissa is proof. Scripture therefore reads, lest He fall upon us with pestilence (Ex. 5:3). There is also a secret regarding the future in the burnt offering. One can also learn from each sacrifice the secret of nature. The purpose of the sin offering and the unleavened bread is to sustain the teachers of the Torah. The reason And the Lord called unto Moses follows And Moses was not able to enter (Ex. 40:35) is that the Glory called to Moses from the tent of meeting and told him to come there, and there He would speak with him. The Glory was on the other side of the curtain and Moses entered there. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture. This is the meaning of and the similitude of the Lord doth he behold (Num. 12:8). The reason Scripture mentions the sacrifices before the commandments is that God’s presence will return to its place if Israel does not keep the law of the burnt offering. The latter came to pass. Far be it from God to require a burnt offering. Scripture clearly states, If I were hungry, I would not tell thee… (Ps. 50:12). On the contrary, it has a secret meaning.

OF YOU. The word mikkem (of you) is placed at the end of the clause. The clause should be read as if written, adam mikkem ki yakriv (when any man of you bringeth an offering). There are many such examples. On the other hand, the word mikkem might mean from your property. The term mikkem might also hint that one is not permitted to bring an offering that is stolen, for Scripture states, I hate robbery with iniquity (Is. 61:8).

OF THE CATTLE. Shall the sacrifice be. This is a general term. Scripture then gives the particulars and states, even of the herd , or of the flock . The flock refers to the species of the sheep and the goat. Your offering is also a general term.
IF HIS OFFERING BE A BURNT–OFFERING. This is a particular. The term olah (burnt offering) is self-explanatory.

OF THE HERD. Fully grown or young but more than eight days. The burnt offering is brought from the choicest animals because it is entirely for God. The male is chosen above the female. Therefore a female animal is not brought for a burnt offering.

WITHOUT BLEMISH. Tammim means without blemish. After stating he shall offer it , Scripture goes on to explain the place where the celebrant is to bring it. It states that he is to enter into the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
BEFORE THE LORD. This is to be understood as connected to he shall bring it to the door of the tent of meeting . THAT HE MAY BE ACCEPTED
BEFORE THE LORD. He shall offer it willingly, not by coercion.

AND HE SHALL LAY HIS HAND. It would appear from the plain meaning of the text that the celebrant lays one hand on the animal about to be sacrificed, for the manner of the scapegoat is unlike all sacrifices. Scripture therefore changed [the manner of the laying of the hands with regard to it]. However, we find that the sages who transmitted the laws to us stated that all “laying” is done with two hands. We rely on them. The body which is offered to atone for that which comes ( ha-olah ) into the mind is called an olah (burnt offering). The sacrifices brought for sins and guilt are also called chattat (sin offering) and asham (guilt offering).
AND IT SHALL BE ACCEPTED FOR HIM. He will obtain favor from God.
TO MAKE ATONEMENT FOR HIM. To serve as a ransom for the punishment due him.
BEFORE THE LORD. Like the burnt offering of the flock, on the side of the altar northward, opposite the table.
The meaning of and he shall kill is that the kohen shall kill. One slaughters and many dash the blood. Scripture clearly states this i.e., and Aaron’s sons delivered unto him the blood (Lev. 9:12).
Scripture states, that is at the door of the tent of meeting because it wants to exclude the altar of incense.
AND HE SHALL FLAY. A kohen or a Levite accompanies him.
AND THE SONS OF AARON THE PRIEST. Levites shall not approach. This commandment was given to the kohanim . Not less than two are required.

AND THE SUET. Many wise men of the generation explain that the word pader (suet) refers to the carcass. However, in my opinion the pader refers to the fat. Our verse is to be understood as follows: And Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces , that is, the pieces of the carcass; and the head, and the suet , that is, the fat. A connective vav is missing from the word ha-rosh (and the head). This is in keeping with the style of the language. Compare, odem pitidah u-vareket (carnelian, topaz, and smargd) (Ex. 28:17). And he shall cut it into its pieces (v. 12) and along with the pieces, its head and its suet. On the other hand, et ha-rosh (and the head) might mean with the head. There are many such instances. The proof of this is: Moses made the head, and the pieces, and the suet smoke (Lev. 8:20).
SHALL LAY THE PIECES. Scripture reads ve-arekhu (shall lay) because it speaks of a bullock, a large animal. Regarding a sheep, Scripture states, and the priest shall lay them (v. 12).
SHALL HE WASH WITH WATER. A kohen or a Levite. Scripture therefore has to add the word kohen to shall make the whole smoke .
A BURNT-OFFERING. The word isheh (burnt offering) is an adjective. It means a fire offering. It describes the word hakol (the whole).
A SWEET SAVOUR. The word nicho’ach (a sweet savour) is self-explanatory.

ON THE SIDE OF THE ALTAR. On the outside. Similarly [ Even mount Zion ], the uttermost part (yarkete) of the north (Ps. 48:3). For many err and say that the tower of Zion was in the midst of Jerusalem.
TURTLE-DOVES. Fully grown, not young.
YOUNG PIGEONS. Scripture reads bene yonah (young pigeons) because it wants to exclude fully grown pigeons. It therefore does not say yonim (pigeons).
PINCH. The word malak (pinch) has no brother in Scripture. We know the laws of “pinching” from our tradition.
AND THE BLOOD THEREOF SHALL BE DRAINED OUT. Ve-nimtzah (shall be drained out) is a nifal . It is related to the word matzit (drained) (Is. 51:17).
ITS CROP. The meaning of murato (its crop) is known. The word more’ah (filthy) in Woe to her that is filthy and polluted (Zeph. 3:1) is similar.
WITH THE FEATHERS THEREOF. The meaning of be-not-zatah is, with the feathers thereof. The word notzah (feathers) in Full of feathers (Ezek. 17:3) is similar.
BESIDE THE ALTAR. On the outside.
ON THE EAST PART. For it is far from the place of the Glory.
IN THE PLACE OF THE ASHES. They shall also place it there.
AND HE SHALL REND IT. The word ve-shissa (and he shall rend it) is related to ve-shosa’at shesa (and is wholly cloven) (Lev. 11:3). The meaning of shissa is split.

AND WHEN ANY ONE BRINGETH. The word nefesh (anyone) means a person. Scripture mentions nefesh because the meal offering is a free will offering and nefesh is called “willing.” Compare, And let a willing spirit uphold me (Ps. 51:14).

FINE FLOUR. The meaning of solet (fine flour) is pure wheat flour. It is the same as that which is called samid in Arabic. Look, it is not fitting that a meal offering brought to the Most High come from anything than which nothing better exists. What is the value of this work today? From an historical and intellectual view, Ibn Ezra’s commentary on the Pentateuch is most important, as explained previously in the preface to Genesis. His influence can be seen in all subsequent Hebrew Biblical commentaries, particularly that of Nahmanides. His influence is equally apparent on Maimonides both in his philosophical work, the Guide of the Perplexed , and his halakhic work, his Mishneh Torah , extending also to many later Biblical scholars and philosophers. All this is well documented in Dr. Strickman’s forewords to the five books of this set. In spite of all of this, however, the question of the English translation’s value still remains. In his introduction to his commentary on the Torah, Ibn Ezra writes, “With regard to verses which deal with laws, statutes and regulations, if we find two possible interpretations for a verse and one of them in keeping with the interpretation of the transmitters of tradition, all of whom were righteous men, then without reservation and with all our might we will rely on the truth of their words. Heaven forbid that we should join the Sadducees who claim that the traditions of the Rabbinic sages contradict the literal meaning of Scripture and the rules of grammar. The fact of the matter is that our ancient sages are true and all their words are true” (Vol. 1, pp. 18,19). However, it must be noted that the rabbis who posited post-Mosaic changes in the Torah were men of stellar reputation. Abarbanel (Num. 21:1) claimed, though his opinion is very questionable, that Nahmanides held such views regarding Num. 21:1-3. Furthermore, despite the fact that Maimonides’ thirteen principles of Judaism ultimately became part of the liturgy and thus were accepted at face value by all pious Jews, in practice not all of Maimonides’ pronouncements on what constitutes heresy were accepted by post-Maimonidian authorities. There was room for difference. For example, according to Maimonides one who directs his or her prayer to anyone but God is guilty of idol worship. Nevertheless, there are prayers that are directed to angels or to God’s attributes. Thus there had to be another reason for normative Judaism’s rejection of the notion of any post-Mosaic changes in the Torah.
AND HE SHALL TAKE. Ve-kamatz (and he shall take) is related to the word li-kematzim (in heaps) (Gen. 41:47). Our sages explained that melo kumtzo means a handful. Their words are true.
OF THE FINE FLOUR THEREOF. A little of it, and so too of the oil. However, he shall burn all of the frankincense.

THE MEMORIAL-PART THEREOF. The alef of azkaratah (the memorial part thereof) is superfluous. Azkaratah is so called because the meal offering by the celebrant serves as a memorial before God. Others say that azkaratah means its scent. It is like scent of the incense. Compare, The scent thereof (zikhro) shall be as the wine of Lebanon (Hos. 14:8).
SHALL BE AARON’S AND HIS SONS’. And to all kohanim equally.
UNLEAVENED CAKES. The word challot (cakes) means thick cakes. Others connect challot to the Rabbinic term chalilah (circle).
A GRIDDLE. Machavat (griddle) refers to a plate covered with a plate. Its tav is in place of a heh , like the tav of ve-shavat (it shall return) in then it shall return to the prince (Ezek. 46:17).
THE STEWING-PAN. Marcheshet (the stewing pan) means fried. Some connect the word marcheshet to rachash (speaks) in My heart speaks (Ps. 45:2). Marcheshet is so called because it emits sounds.
AARON’S AND HIS SONS’. After him. That is, to the kohen who places it upon the fire, for Scripture states so with regard to the two meal offerings.

LEAVEN. Se’or refers to leaven. It is the same case with honey. Some say that our verse speaks of date honey. The same is true whenever Scripture speaks of a land flowing with milk and honey . There is what appears to be proof of their opinion in the Book of Ezra.

AS AN OFFERING OF FIRST-FRUITS YE MAY BRING THEM UNTO THE LORD. As the two wave-loaves of two tenth parts of an ephah which were waved before God on the festival of Shavu’ot (Lev. 23:17). The meaning of unto the Lord is, even though they are holy unto the Lord they are food for the kohen .
THE COVENANT OF THY GOD. God caused you to enter the covenant and made you swear that you would not offer anything which is unsalted and inedible, for that is an insult.

AND IF THOU BRING A MEAL-OFFERING OF FIRSTFRUITS. Many say that the word im (if) indicates an obligation. I believe that there is no need for this explanation, for there is an obligation to bring the first of the grain and not the first grain. One who wishes to bring a meal offering from the first grain as a free will offering may do so.
CORN IN THE EAR. Aviv (com in the ear) is so called because it is first. It is related to the word av (father).

GROATS. The meaning of geres (groats) is known. It is close to being related to the word garesah (breaketh) in My soul breaketh (Ps. 119:20). The latter is so even though the word garesah is spelled with a samekh .
FRESH EAR. The word karmel (fresh ear) is related to the word karmel (fresh ears) in and fresh ears of corn in his sack (II Kings 4:42).
PEACE-OFFERINGS. The term shelamim (peace offerings) is self-explanatory.
BY THE LOINS. The meaning of the term kesalim (loins) is known. It is related to the word kesilehem (constellations thereof) in and the constellations thereof (Is . 13:10).

HARD BY THE KIDNEYS. The term al (hard by) means with, as in And they came, both men with (al) women (Ex. 35:22). Kelayot (kidneys) are so called because they are the source of lust and sex. The word kelayot is related to the word kaletah (pineth) in My soul yearneth, yea, even pineth (Ps. 84:3).

THE FAT THEREOF, THE FAT TAIL ENTIRE. The meaning of chelbo ha-alyah temimah (the fat thereof, the fat tail entire) is, the fat as it is, for the tail is called fat. The Sadducees, as I will explain to you in the next Torah portion, err. The Gaon also errs, for he says that chelbo haalyah is to be interpreted as the fat thereof and the tail. The latter is contrary to the rules of grammar, for the phrase should have read chelbo ve-alyato (its fat and its tail) or hachelev ve-ha-alyah (and its tail and its fat).
THE RUMP-BONE. The meaning of atzeh (rump-bone) is known from its context. It has no brother. There is a commentator who far-fetchedly connected it to the word etz (tree).
THE FOOD OF THE OFFERING MADE BY FIRE. I have previously explained that the meaning of lechem is food. It is found in reference to fruit and meat.

AND IF HIS OFFERING BE A GOAT. Any animal classified as a goat, be it male or female, as is the case with a sheep. Scripture does not mention the fat tail with regard to the herd. It only mentions it with regard to the lamb because the tail of a goat or a bull is small. Furthermore, the lambs in the Land of Israel have a large tail. The latter is well known.

ALL THE FAT IS THE LORD’S. This is a general statement. Now, since the fat and the blood belong to God, they are prohibited to you. I will expostulate at length on the phrase a perpetual statute in the next Torah portion.

IF ANY ONE SHALL SIN. By inadvertently transgressing one of the negative commandments, the penalty for which is excision or flogging [for a deliberate act]. The word nefesh (any one) takes in Israelites and strangers, for it is so stated. Scripture then goes into detail. It begins with the kohen gadol , the anointed kohen .

TO BRING GUILT ON THE PEOPLE. The kohen gadol taught incorrectly and the people were guilty, all of them having acted inadvertently. On the other hand, the meaning of leashmat ha-am (to bring guilt on the people) might be, because of the guilt of all of the people. It is mentioned here because the kohen is the bearer of the Torah and he is very careful and holy unto God.
FOR HIS SIN. Al chattato (for his sin) means because of his sin. Since the kohen gadol is great he must offer a bullock, which is the largest animal of all that are offered on the altar.

AND THE PRIEST SHALL DIP. The anointed kohen himself. You will find the reason for seven times in the Torah portion Va-Yar Balak (Num. 22:2-25:9). The kohen gadol sprinkles some of the blood of the sin offering in front of the veil of the sanctuary and on the incense altar because of his exalted status. The kohen gadol burns the entire bullock, aside from the various fats, outside [of the camp] because it is not a burnt offering.
WHERE THE ASHES ARE POURED OUT. It should be burned in the place where the ashes of the altar are found.

WHEN THE SIN WHEREIN THEY HAVE SINNED IS KNOWN. The same law, even though it is not mentioned, applies to the kohen gadol , for if the sin not be known to the kohen gadol , then he does not bring a sin offering. Others say that the kohen gadol shall bring this sacrifice every year because he may have sinned. Scripture mentions the sin…is known with regard to the whole congregation of Israel, for it is possible that the kohen will inform them. However, there is no one to inform the kohen; he informs himself. The sin offering of the congregation is the same as that of the kohen gadol in all details. The kohen gadol is thus equivalent to all of Israel.
AND THE ELDERS OF THE CONGREGATION. The elders are the leaders. They will lay their hands on their behalf and on behalf of all of Israel, for it is impossible for all of Israel to place their hands.
IT IS THE SIN-OFFERING. The bullock. If Israel errs and they do not do one of the positive commandments, then they shall bring a bullock as a burnt offering and a he-goat as a sin offering.

WHEN A RULER SINNETH. The words are inverted. Our verse should be read as if written, when the sinner is the ruler. It is connected to that which is written above, that is, And if the whole congregation of Israel… (v. 13). Our verse, as it were, states, and if the one who sins is the ruler of a tribe or the ruler of a father’s house.

IF HIS SIN…BE KNOWN TO HIM. Scripture employs an abridged style. It is similar to the verse dealing with the kohen . Its meaning is, if the ruler knows on his own that he has sinned or someone else who has seen him makes it known to him. The following is the grammatical explanation of hoda elav (be known to him): Hoda (be known) is a verb in the perfect. Compare, ve-hetzar lekha (and he shall besiege thee) (Deut. 28:52). The one who informs is omitted. Compare, whom she bore (Num. 26:59). Rabbi Moses the Kohen says that hoda (be known) is a hofal , for the cholam and the shuruk interchange. Hoda follows the paradigm of hurad (was brought down) in And Joseph was brought down to Egypt (Gen. 39:1). The ruler offers a he-goat as a sacrifice in keeping with The greyhound ; the he-goat also (Prov. 30:31). The latter is in accordance with the interpretation of the Gaon in the Book of Proverbs. The offering consists of a male, in keeping with the status of the ruler. However, its blood is not brought inside of the sanctuary. The kohanim , as is stated in Scripture, eat of the ruler’s sin offering to atone for the ruler. The kohen gadol does not eat of his sin offering.
OF THE COMMON PEOPLE. The reference is to all of Israel, the ordinary kohanim and the Levites.
AND BE GUILTY. Ashem (guilty) is a verb in the perfect. It is like zaken (was old) in when Isaac was old (Gen. 27:1).
A GOAT, A FEMALE. For his status is lower than that of the ruler.
I will explain the meaning of ve-nislach lo (and he shall be forgiven) (v. 26) in the Torah portion Send Thou (Num. 13:1).
AND IF HE BRING A LAMB. If he brings a sin offering from the lamb species then he shall bring a female, as in the case of the she-goat.
[AS THE FAT OF THE LAMB IS TAKEN AWAY.] Scripture states the aforementioned because it wants to indicate that one is to offer the fat tail, for a she-goat has no fat tail.

AND IF ANY ONE SIN, IN THAT HE HEARETH THE VOICE OF ADJURATION. Alah (adjuration) refers to a curse. Similarly alit (thou didst utter a curse) in about which thou didst utter a curse (Jud. 17:2). Scripture employs an abridged style. Scripture warns that the witness is obligated to testify, for if he does not testify then he is liable for punishment from God, for he bears his iniquity. If he forgets and does not testify and then reminds himself [then he brings a guilt offering].
OR IF ANY ONE TOUCH ANY UNCLEAN THING. [WHETHER IT BE THE CARCASS OF AN UNCLEAN BEAST.] The reference is to the carcass of any of the four mentioned, namely, the swine and his compatriots.
OR THE CARCASS OF UNCLEAN CATTLE. Unclean for food such as horses or asses. The carcass of unclean swarming things refers to the carcass of the eight swarming things mentioned in Scripture.

IT BEING HIDDEN FROM HIM. He learned of this afterwards. [3. OR IF HE TOUCH THE UNCLEANNESS OF MAN.] He touched a man that suffered a flux, or someone who was unclean because he touched a dead body, or a woman who suffered from a flux, or a menstruant.
UTTER CLEARLY WITH AN OATH. Le-vatte visefatayim (utter clearly) means to utter with the lips.

TO DO EVIL. To a guilty person, or, as the Gaon explains, to fast. Scripture mentions these sins because the violator is obligated to confess these sins. He is not obligated to confess before the kohen for other sins which consist of the violation of negative commandments. The sacrifice is the same.
AND IF HIS MEANS SUFFICE NOT. For all manner of work is done by the hand. It is the means by which one acquires. The clause alludes to one who does not have the means.

ONE FOR A SIN-OFFERING, AND THE OTHER FOR A BURNT-OFFERING. Rabbi Isaac says the reason that one bird is brought for a burnt offering is that an unseemly thought may have entered his mind because his means do not suffice. However, I believe that the bird brought as an offering corresponds to the organs of the sacrifice offered on the altar. The second bird is a sin offering, as the law requires.
THE TENTH PART OF AN EPHAH. The amount of food a person eats in one day.

COMMIT A TRESPASS. The reference is to something which covered the offender. Timol ma’al (commit a trespass) is related to the word me’il (garment). The reason why he shall bring a ram worth silver shekels is that he sinned against that which is sanctified to God. The minimum of the plural shekalim (shekels) is two.

HE SHALL MAKE RESTITUTION. He shall make restitution for sinning by using a holy object and add a fifth. This is a guilt offering brought by one who errs at first and then becomes cognizant of his sin.

AND IF ANY ONE SIN. And violates one of the negative commandments and does not know that what he did is prohibited, he shall bring a ram. Many believe that the ram is brought as a “doubt guilt offering.” He brings a ram if he does not know whether he violated the law or not. A sin offering is brought if he did not know that he sinned and then became aware of it. Observe, a sin offering is brought if he did not know that a certain act is prohibited until he was informed of it. A guilt offering is brought if he knew that it is prohibited but forgot, and then reminded himself. On the other hand, our verse might be speaking of a “doubt guilt offering.”
HE IS CERTAINLY GUILTY BEFORE THE LORD. This explains why it is called a guilt offering. It is so called because he is guilty.
AND COMMIT A TRESPASS AGAINST THE LORD. By violating one of the negative precepts governing the relationship between a man and his neighbor.
IN A MATTER OF DEPOSIT. Partnership. He joined hands with him.
OR OF ROBBERY. Involving force. Compare, and plucked (va-yigzol) the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand (I Chron. 11:23).
OR HAVE OPPRESSED. In secret.
HIS NEIGHBOR. Amito means his neighbor. It most probably means the one who is beside him.

AND SWEAR TO A LIE. The meaning of ve-nishba al shaker (and swear to a lie) is, or swear to a lie regarding money that one seeks from him. The fact that Scripture states, or any thing about which he has sworn falsely (v. 24) is proof of this. The heh of va-hennah (therein) is superfluous.
IN FULL. Be-rosho (in full) means in itself, or its worth.
THE FIFTH PART. The minimum of a plural is two. Thus chamishitav (the fifth part) means two fifths. I will explain it later.
IN THE DAY OF HIS BEING GUILTY. Its meaning is, in the day that he turns away from his guilt he shall bring a ram.

ACCORDING TO THY VALUATION. As the first one. Scripture adds fifths because this guilt offering is brought for a deliberate sin. There is an individual opinion that this guilt offering is also a “doubt-offering.”
TO BE GUILTY THEREBY. Ashmah (guilty) is a noun in the kal . Scripture employs it in place of the infinite.

IT IS THAT WHICH GOETH UP. The burnt offering is called an olah because it is entirely consumed ( olah ) on the altar. Scripture here hints that the olah should not be offered at night but rather that it shall be on its firewood until the morning. The heh of mokedah (its firewood) is superfluous. On the other hand, moked and mokedah may be two nouns.
AND THE FIRE OF THE ALTAR SHALL BE KEPT BURNING THEREBY. Not outside.
HIS LINEN GARMENT. The word middo means a garment. The wise men said that it is a garment in keeping with his size.
UPON HIS FLESH. Flesh alludes to the genitals. Similarly an issue out of his flesh (Lev. 15:2).
WHERETO THE FIRE HATH CONSUMED. Which remains from what the fire consumes.
BESIDE THE ALTAR. Outside of the eastern side.
AND THE FIRE UPON THE ALTAR SHALL BE KEPT BURNING THEREBY. Scripture repeats itself in order to add it shall not go out during the day.
The meaning of ba-boker ba-boker is, every morning. The kohen shall first offer the burnt offering and then the organs of the peace offering.
FIRE SHALL BE KEPT BURNING UPON THE ALTAR CONTINUALLY. This verse was written in order to add the word continually .

SHALL OFFER IT. Hakrev (shall offer) is an infinitive. The meaning of hakrev otah bene aharon is, the sons of Aaron shall offer it. This means that one of the sons of Aaron shall offer it. Scripture therefore reads, And he shall take up there-from (v. 8). This section adds to that which is written in the portion Va-Yikra .
IT SHALL BE EATEN WITHOUT LEAVEN IN A HOLY PLACE. Note, Scripture adds two commandments. Every male (v. 11) is a third.
[IT SHALL NOT BE BAKED WITH LEAVEN.] This is the principal rule regarding the Passover matzot .
AS THE SIN-OFFERING, AND AS THE GUILT-OFFERING. So too the meal offering.
WHATSOEVER TOUCHETH THEM SHALL BE HOLY. Whatever touches the meal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering shall be holy unto God.
THIS IS THE OFFERING OF AARON. Or one of his sons who takes his place.

IN THE DAY WHEN…ANOINTED. When the anointing oil is poured upon his head. Some say that the bet of be-yom (in the day) is in place of a mem . Its meaning is, from the day that he is anointed he has to regularly bring his meal offering.

WHEN IT IS SOAKED. Murbekhet (when it is soaked) has no brother. Some say it means soft. Others say that murbekhet means quickly. The tav of tevi’ennah (thou shalt bring it) is directed at Aaron. Similarly the tav of takriv (thou shalt offer). I believe that this is also true of the tav of tufine (in broken pieces). It means to fix. It has no neighbor. The ancients said that tufine is a combination of the two words, te’afeh and na (it shall be baked raw). Rabbi Jonah the grammarian says that tufine follows the paradigm of dukhifat (hoopoe) (Lev. 11:19). This is a distorted form.
WHOLLY. The word kalil means wholly. It shall be wholly sacrificed unto God.
IT SHALL NOT BE EATEN. As all the meal offerings are, for how can a kohen eat his meal or sin offering. The place of the slaughter of all the sin offerings was in the north.
IT IS MOST HOLY. It is like one of the other holy things.

THE PRIEST THAT OFFERETH IT FOR SIN. Ha-kohen ha-mechatte (the priest that offereth it for sin) means the kohen who sprinkles the blood. Ha-kohen ha-mechatte is another way of saying the kohen that removes the sin of the sinner. Many of the commentaries say that ha-mechatte means who washes or cleans. The word techatteni (purge me) in Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean (Ps. 51:9) is similar.

WHATSOEVER SHALL TOUCH. Whatsoever shall touch the flesh of the sin offering will be holy unto God, and the kohen shall eat it. The portion of the kohen who sprinkles the blood of the sin offering is therefore like the portion of all his brothers.

IS SPRINKLED. Rabbi Mosheh Ha-Kohen says that yizzeh (is sprinkled) is similar to the word yitteh (shall…bend) (Job 15:29). It is a kal . When the yod is vocalized with a pattach it is a hifil . The swallowed letter is a nun . We similarly find the word va-yiz (and…was sprinkled) in and some of her blood was sprinkled (II Kings 9:33) vocalized with a chirik , and vayaz with a pattach . However, the word natah (turned) is vocalized with a tzereh in the kal . We similarly find ve-yez nitzcham (and their lifeblood is dashed) (Is. 63:3). He explained it very well.

The Lord commanded that the place where some of the blood of the sin offering fell on the garment be washed because the sin offering is holy. [IN A HOLY PLACE.] The reference is to the courtyard of the tent of meeting, for there is a difference between holy and clean.

THAT WHEREON IT WAS SPRINKLED. The word “place” or the word “or” is missing. It means: Or if someone shall sprinkle upon it, that is, upon the flesh, then the kohen shall wash the flesh and then eat it. On the other hand, its meaning might be, the place where the blood is sprinkled shall be washed. In this case the word beged (garment) is both masculine and feminine. The word yado (his hand) in even as his hand can afford (Lev. 14:31) is similar. The tav of tekhabbes (thou shalt wash) is directed to the kohen .

WHEREIN IT IS SODDEN. Bushalah (sodden), morak (scoured), and shuttaf (rinsed) are all pu’als. Morak is vocalized with a cholam because of the resh which, except in a few places, does not receive a dagesh . Morak follows the paradigm of zorak (dashed) in was not dashed against him (Num. 19:13). Morak is related to the word mirku (furbish) in Furbish the spears ( Jer . 46:4), for the mem of morak is a root letter.

[IT IS MOST HOLY.] Scripture states it is most holy with regard to every male because only the perfect may eat from a sin offering whose organs are offered and is brought for atonement for sins. Males are more perfect than females. Even a small child is called a male. A male who is thirteen years old [is considered an adult] as our fathers have transmitted.

AND NO SIN-OFFERING, WHEREOF ANY OF THE BLOOD IS BROUGHT INTO…THE HOLY PLACE. Note, the place of the “veil” is called holy, for the courtyard, even though it is holy, is not holy in comparison to the tent of meeting. Observe, the inside of the curtain is called holy in comparison to the tent of meeting. Compare, Herewith shall Aaron come into the holy place (Lev. 16:3). The sin offering spoken of in our verse is the sin offering of the kohen gadol or of the congregation.

AND THIS IS THE LAW OF THE GUILT-OFFERING. I have previously explained to you the difference between a sin offering and a guilt offering. [There is a difference between the two] even though Scripture employs the term guilt when referring to a sin offering and the word sin when referring to a guilt offering. Scripture records this section because it wants to make mention of the fat, to which no reference is made when Scripture earlier records the law of the sin offering.

ANY MAN’S BURNT-OFFERING. The word olat (burnt offering) is penultimately accented in accordance with the rules of Hebrew grammar. It is so accented because the word that follows has the accent on the first part of the word.
Scripture reads to himself even though it earlier stated even the priest because it wants to further explain that the skin not be given to another kohen .

AND ALL THAT IS DRESSED. The word na’asah (dressed) is an adjective in the feminine. It is like the word nirah (seen) in there was no stone seen (I Kings 6:18). The masculine form of the word is found in Now that which was prepared (na’aseh) (Neh. 5:18).
OR DRY. As in the case of the “descending” meal offering and a meal offering brought about because of jealousy.
IF HE OFFER IT FOR A THANKSGIVING. Its meaning is, if he offers it because he wants to give thanks to God for escaping from some trouble.
UNLEAVENED CAKE. As many as he desires. However, he cannot bring fewer than two. The same applies to the unleavened wafers.

SOAKED. I believe that the best interpretation of solet murbekhet (fine flour soaked) is chosen flour. The unleavened cakes and the wafers were baked. The cakes made from chosen flour were not so treated.
WITH CAKES. The meaning of al challot is with cakes. Similarly And they came, both men and (al) women (Ex. 35:22).
AND OF IT HE SHALL PRESENT ONE OUT OF EACH OFFERING. Note, there had to be a minimum of four unleavened cakes. However, in truth there were ten.

SHALL BE EATEN ON THE DAY OF HIS OFFERING. The one who offers the sacrifice, his family, and all who are clean shall eat it, for the peace offerings are also holy even though they are lesser holy offerings.
A VOW. A vow uttered by the lips when in trouble.
OR A FREEWILL-OFFERING. His sprit moved him to bring a sacrifice to God, not because he had made a vow, or for thanksgiving.
ON THE DAY THAT HE OFFERETH HIS SACRIFICE. The word hakrivo is an infinitive in the hifil . [AND ON THE MORROW.] On the morrow of that day.

[THAT WHICH REMAINETH.] The vav of ve-ha-notar (that which remaineth) has the same meaning as an unaspirated fa in Arabic. The same applies to the vav in va-ya’azov (left) in left his servants (Ex. 9:21) and the vav in ve-ha-aretz (now the earth) in Now the earth was unformed and void (Gen. 1:2).
SHALL BE BURNT WITH FIRE. Like the parts of a sacrifice which Scripture designates for burning. However, it should not be burned on the altar.

[NEITHER SHALL IT BE IMPUTED UNTO HIM THAT OFFERETH IT.] Its meaning is, since Scripture designates that specific parts of the sacrifice be offered to God, all that remains of the animal is holy. Similarly the stones of the altar. Since they are holy, it is unfit that anything that remains from them be used in a non-sacred way. Scripture therefore reads, of unhewn stones (Deut. 27:6).

ABHORRED. The word piggul (abhorred) is to be rendered as the Aramaic translator does. Similarly the word piggulim (abominable things) in And broth of abominable things is in their vessels (Is. 65:4). Some ask, “Since the sweet savor ascended, how can it not be accepted?” The answer is that it depends on his intention. According to the law, the peace offerings must be holy. However that which is abhorred is not holy. Furthermore, the celebrant’s gain disappears in his loss with regard to a peace offering. In the case of a vow offering, there is a new sin corresponding to the first if he does not fulfil his vow.
SHALL BEAR HIS INIQUITY. His punishment. Scripture does not mention the punishment. One who is unclean and eats sacred flesh is punished with karet (excision).

[HAVING HIS UNCLEANLINESS.] This means if his uncleanliness comes from his body, as in the case of a flux or a leper. Also because of uncleanliness caused by a nocturnal emission, as Scripture states, for he thought: Something hath befallen him (I Sam. 20:26). It also applies to uncleanliness that comes from contact with an outside source such as a dead body, or a living person who experienced a flux or is a leper, or an unclean beast which may not be eaten, or a detestable thing from among the fowl and that which swarms. A Sadducee once came to me and asked, “Does the Torah prohibit the fat tail?” I answered that it is true that the fat tail is called “fat” ( chelev ), for the Torah states, the fat thereof, the fat tail entire (Lev. 3:9). However, while our sages prohibited all fat, they permitted the fat tail. The Sadducee then replied, “Does not the Torah prohibit all fat? Indeed it is written, that ye shall eat neither fat nor blood (Lev. 3:17). The latter is preceded by Scripture’s statement, It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations ( Ibid. ).”I once again answered him that this verse relates to the peace offering. Also, the clause It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations does not provide complete proof, for we see that Scripture states, And ye shall eat neither bread, nor parched corn, nor fresh ears, until this selfsame day, until ye have brought the offering of your God (Lev. 23:14). Now Scripture there writes, it is a statute for ever ( Ibid. ). Shall we then not eat bread in the Diaspora? For we have not brought the omer offering. He, on his part, replied, “ Ye shall eat no fat, of ox, or sheep, or goat (v. 23).” I again answered that this verse too refers to a peace offering. For whosoever eateth the fat of the beast, of which men present an offering (v. 25) is proof, for the latter excludes the fat of all flesh which is not offered as a peace offering, that is, all secular meat. Scripture therefore states in our section, And the fat of that which dieth of itself, and the fat of that which is torn of beasts, may be used for any other service; but ye shall in no wise eat of it (v. 24). It is known that the flesh of that which dies of itself and that which is torn of beasts is prohibited. It is the flesh that is prohibited. Now since the fat is not offered on the altar, one might think that it is permitted. Hence Scripture warns, but ye shall in no wise eat of it . It is for this reason that Scripture does not mention the blood. This section was written in order to explain the punishment incurred by one who eats the fat of sacred flesh. The verse relating to any blood (v. 27) was similarly written to add that the blood of fowl is prohibited. The fat of fowl is therefore permitted. Scripture’s statement in the Book of Deuteronomy (Deut. 1:1) with regard to meat eaten out of desire, that is, non-sacred meat (Deut. 12:15-25), is total proof of what I say, for Scripture states that non-sacred meat may be eaten in its entirety. Only its blood is excluded in three places. Fat is totally unmentioned. The Sadducee’s eyes opened and he uttered an oath with his lips to the effect that he will never rely on his judgment when it comes to explaining the commandments. He will rely only on the tradition transmitted by the Pharisees.
THE RIGHT THIGH. Is to be given to the kohen who sprinkles the blood, and the breast to all the kohanim .
THIS IS THE CONSECRATED PORTION. This is the reward of the consecration of Aaron or of the consecration of his sons. The word mishchat (consecrated portion) means leadership.
IN THE DAY THAT THEY WERE ANOINTED. Be-yom (in the day) is to be rendered, from the day. Similarly ba-basar u-va-lachem (of the flesh and of the bread) (Lev. 8:32).
AND OF THE CONSECRATION-OFFERING. As written in the Torah portion And Thou Shalt Command (Ex. 27:20).

TO PRESENT THEIR OFFERINGS UNTO THE LORD, IN THE WILDERNESS OF SINAI. For Israel did not offer sacrifices until they came to Mount Sinai. I have previously shown you that the altar which Moses built after defeating Amalek was built in Horeb, which is Mount Sinai. Israel camped there for a year minus ten days. The latter is clearly stated in Scripture. They did not offer sacrifices in the wilderness, for the prophet clearly states, Did ye bring unto Me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel ? (Amos 5:25). Israel similarly only offered the Passover sacrifice in Egypt, and for a second time at Mount Sinai, for they had no cattle in the wilderness. They did not circumcise on the way after they journeyed from Mount Sinai. Most of them were thus uncircumcised. Joshua circumcised them so that they could partake of the Passover sacrifice.

AND THE BULLOCK OF THE SIN-OFFERING. The word chattat (sin offering) has a heh prefixed to it because the sin offering is mentioned earlier. The same applies to the heh prefixed to elim (rams) and matzot (unleavened bread).
ALL THE CONGREGATION. The heads of the tribes and the elders.
AND MOSES BROUGHT AARON. To the laver ( kiyyor ).
AND WASHED THEM. By command.

AND BOUND IT UNTO HIM. The word va-yepod means and girded. Just as the golden plate ( tzitz ) (v. 9) is not the mitre ( mitznefet ) ( Ibid .), so the Urim and the Thummim (v. 8) are not the stones of the breastplate (Ex. 28:15-21). Similarly, the Tablets were placed in the ark. Scripture therefore reads, And in the breastplate he put in the Urim and the Thummim (v. 8).
AND MOSES TOOK THE ANOINTING OIL. It means that Moses had taken the oil before the anointing of Aaron.

AND MOSES BROUGHT AARON’S SONS. Scripture notes this a second time because it speaks at length. On the other hand, this means that when Moses brought Aaron’s sons he dressed them in tunics. The word va-yalbishem (and clothed them) is a verb that governs two actions.
AND PURIFIED. I have previously explained this.
AND SANCTIFIED IT. So that all the sins may be atoned upon it.

AND HE TOOK ALL THE FAT THAT WAS UPON THE INWARDS. Scripture earlier stated, the fat that covereth the inwards (Lev. 7:3) Another verse states, the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards (Lev. 3:3). Note, the fat that covereth [ the inwards ] is substantial. However, the fat that is upon the inwards consists of a little from here and there. That which covereth [ the inwards ] is also upon the inwards . Hence Scripture employed abridged terminology.

WERE BURNT WITH FIRE. Some say by Moses himself. Others say by the command of Moses. They offer as proof, as the Lord commanded Moses (v. 21). However, this is no proof, for that is the style of the Hebrew language.

AND THE OTHER RAM WAS PRESENTED, THE RAM OF CONSECRATION, AND AARON AND HIS SONS LAID (VA-YISMEKHU) THEIR HANDS. The first verse reads, and Aaron and his sons laid (ve-samakh) (v. 14). Note, contra a great grammarian who erred, there is no difference between ve-samakh aron u-vanav (and Aaron and his sons laid) (v. 14) and va-yismekhu aron u-vanav (and Aaron and his sons laid). The grammarian said that ve-samakh indicates that Aaron alone shall lay hands, and then his sons. Vesamekhu means, and they shall all lay together.

RIGHT EAR. Ha-yemanit (right) is similar to ha-penimit (inner). The meaning of al tenukh (upon the tip) and bohen (toe) will be explained in the section This Shall Be the Law (Lev. 14:2). Note, the blood atones for Aaron’s life. Similarly for it is the blood that maketh atonement by reason of the life (Lev. 17:11). This means the life in the blood shall atone. Life is thus offered for life. Then [Zipporah]… cast it at his feet (Ex. 4:25) has a similar explanation.

ONE UNLEAVENED CAKE. The reference is to the one loaf (kikkar) of bread (Ex. 29:2s). It is possible that the term kikkar (loaf) refers to weight. It is not the same weight as that of a kikkar (talent) of gold or silver.

AND PLACED THEM ON THE FAT. Scripture does not mention the lobe of the liver and the kidneys, for the lobe was small. The meaning of yoteret (lobe) is similar to the meaning of the word yitron (profit) in What profit hath man (Eccles. 1:3). The kidneys are offered with their fat, for Scripture would not refer to the kidneys as fat. Only the fat tail is fat.
AND WAVED THEM. Moses waved Aaron and his sons as Aaron waved the Levites.
BOIL THE FLESH. Aaron and his sons themselves were to boil the flesh, for and seethe its flesh (Ex. 29:31) is by command.
AND THAT WHICH REMAINETH OF THE FLESH AND OF THE BREAD. Until the morning, for Scripture so states.

HE SHALL CONSECRATE YOU. The word ketz (end) was omitted. Our verse should be read as if written, at the end of seven days. On the other hand, its meaning might be, for a period of seven days. Some say that And ye shall not go out…seven days indicates that they went out at night for their needs. However, I believe that they went out during the day and night for their needs. A great scholar said that they dug a pit in the courtyard of the tent of meeting. However, this is farfetched. Scripture states, And the children of Israel wept for Moses…thirty days (Deut. 34:8), as if there was no moment that they did not weep. Scripture clearly states that they shall sit at the door of the tent of meeting day and night (v. 35). Its meaning is that they shall not occupy themselves with any matter and they should not go to another place. Similarly neither shall he go out of the sanctuary (Lev. 21:12), as I will explain.

AS HATH BEEN DONE THIS DAY. This means, as Moses did on this day, so God commanded to be done during the seven days of consecration. Scripture should have read, as I did. However, such is the style of the holy tongue. Compare, Thus shall Ezekiel he unto you (Ezek. 24:24); and Jephthah, and Samuel (I Sam. 12:11). The fact that Scripture states, So the Lord hath commanded to do (v. 34); And thus shall you do unto Aaron, and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded thee; seven days (Ex. 29:35) is proof of this. Furthermore, Scripture states, And every day shalt thou offer the bullock of sin-offering (Ex. 29:36). The latter is similar to two day by day , for a continual burnt-offering (Num. 28:3). Scripture there writes, and thou shalt do the purification upon the altar…and thou shalt anoint it ( Ibid. ) every day until the end of the days of consecration. Furthermore, Scripture states, Seven days thou shalt make atonement for the altar (Ex. 29:37). It does not mention the two rams because Scripture employed an abridged style. Many are of the opinion that Moses was to offer a bullock of sin offering alone every day. I believe that the reason Scripture mentions the bullock is that the blood of the burnt offering ram was to be placed on Aaron and his sons, and the second ram’s flesh was to be eaten. However, the sin offering bullock was to consecrate the altar. Scripture clearly states, al hakippurim (beside the other offerings of atonement) (Ex. 29:36), the meaning of which is, for atonement.
AND AT THE DOOR OF THE TENT OF MEETING SHALL YE ABIDE. This is stated once again in order to add, that ye die not .

I AM COMMANDED. Tzuvveti (I am commanded) is a pu’al . Some say that the meaning of for so I am commanded is identical to according to all that I have commanded thee (Ex. 29:35), even though Scripture does not state there that they are to abide at the front of the tent of meeting.

AND IT CAME TO PASS ON THE EIGHTH DAY. It would have appeared to us that the eighth day is the eighth day of Nisan, for the tabernacle was erected on the first day of the month. However, the transmitters of tradition said that the reference is to the first of Nisan. Moses erected and took apart the tabernacle on each one of the seven days of consecration to train and teach.
THAT MOSES CALLED AARON AND HIS SONS. And they went out from the opening of the tent of meeting. On the other hand, the congregation entered the courtyard.

A BULL-CALF. During the seven days of consecration a bullock and also a ram were offered for a burnt offering. Scripture does not mention whether the bull-calf was “of the year.” It appears to me that a bullock and a bull-calf are one and the same when the term “year” is unmentioned.

WITHOUT BLEMISH. This refers to the bull-calf and the ram. The bullocks of consecration were to purify the altar. This bull-calf was to atone ( le-khapper ) for Aaron. I have already explained this word.
A HE-GOAT FOR A SIN-OFFERING. For the congregation. Also [for the congregation] a calf that has not reached the age of a complete year, and a lamb for a burnt offering.
AND AN OX AND A RAM. Fully grown.
AND A MEAL-OFFERING. Of fine flour for each and every one.

[6. AND MOSES SAID.] Va-yomer mosheh (and Moses said) is to be understood in a manner similar to that of va-eshal otah (and I asked her) (Gen. 24:47). I have pointed out to you how the latter is to be interpreted. The meaning of our clause is that Moses had already said to them, This is the thing which the Lord commanded that ye should do , namely, that you offer a he-goat (v. 3), a calf (v. 3), a lamb (v. 3), and an ox and a ram (v. 4); then the glory of God will then appear to them. The latter refers to the fire that came forth from the Lord.

AND MAKE ATONEMENT FOR THYSELF, AND FOR THE PEOPLE. There is a divine command that you make atonement for yourself and for all of the people. You will atone for yourself with a sin offering bullock. Afterwards you will atone for the congregation by offering the people’s sacrifice, for a person cannot atone for another unless he has been purified from all sin.
WHICH WAS FOR HIMSELF. It came from his own property. So too the bullock of the Day of Atonement.
THE BLOOD. He poured out the blood which remained.
BUT THE FAT. Which covered the innards, which was upon the innards, and which was on the kidneys.
AND…DELIVERED UNTO HIM The word va-yamtzi’u (and…delivered unto him) is related to the word matza (found). Aaron found the blood when it was needed.
AND THE PEOPLE’S OFFERING WAS PRESENTED. On the altar.
AND OFFERED IT FOR SIN, AS THE FIRST. This refers to the sin offering bull-calf.
The meaning of va-yechattehu (and offered it for sin) is, to atone with it for the sin.
AND THEY PUT THE FAT. With the kidneys and the lobe of the liver, as I have shown you.
AND THE BREASTS. The breast of the ox and the breast of the ram.
AND THE RIGHT THIGH. From this one and that one. The word shok (thigh) is connected to the word ha-pe’ah (corner), or ha-tazad (side).
AND AARON LIFTED UP HIS HANDS TOWARD THE PEOPLE. Toward them. From here our ancients transmitted to us the form taken by the “raising of the hands.”

AND HE CAME DOWN. Va-yered (and he came down) is to be understood in accordance with what I have previously pointed out to you many times. It means that Aaron had already come down from offering the people’s sin offering, burnt offering, and peace offering.

Scripture reads came down because the altar was three cubits in height. After this, Moses and Aaron came to the tent of meeting. It is likely that they came to pray that a fire would come forth. When they came out both of them blessed the people.
THE BURNT-OFFERING. The burnt offering of Aaron, the burnt offering of the people, and the continual burnt offering, for Scripture states, beside the burnt-offering of the morning (Num. 28:23).
AND THE FAT. From the bull-calf and the ram of Aaron, and the he-goat, the ox, and the ram
THEY SHOUTED. Va-yaronnu (they shouted) means they raised their voices. Compare, rinnah (cry) in And there went a cry throughout the host (I Kings 22:36).
EACH OF THEM HIS CENSER. Each man took his firepan. I believe that this event also took place on the eighth day. Behold, this day have they offered their sin-offering (v. 19) is proof of this.
AND PUT FIRE THEREIN. Not from the fire that came forth from the Lord. This is the meaning of strange fire .
[WHICH HE HAD NOT COMMANDED THEM.] They acted on their own and were not commanded to burn incense and certainly not to employ a strange fire.
AND THEY DIED BEFORE THE LORD. They thought that they were doing something favorable before Him.

THIS IS THAT THE LORD SPOKE. God has previously told me that He will demonstrate His holiness through those who are close to Him. Our verse is similar in meaning to You only have I known (Amos 3:2). I will be exalted when I show My sanctity through those who are close to Me. I will then be glorified before all the people, and they will fear me.

CARRY YOUR BRETHREN FROM BEFORE THE SANCTUARY. Some say that the incense was before the altar of the burnt offering and the Levites entered there. Others say that the incense was on the altar of incense and Moses took them out of the tent of meeting.
FROM BEFORE THE SANCTUARY. The reference is to the courtyard. The latter, as I have explained, is referred to as the sanctuary, in contrast to the camp.
LET NOT THE HAIR OF YOUR HEADS GO LOOSE. Some say that tifra’u (go loose) means to let the hair grow long.

REND. The word tifromu means rend. Actually the word tifra’u (go loose) is related to the word faru’a (go loose) in his clothes shall be rent, and the hair of his head shall go loose (Lev. 13:45). Many say that it means covered. Others say that it means uncovered. The words of tradition are true.

THAT YE DIE NOT. The word ve-lo (that…not) is to be read as if written twice. Compare, And I have not learned wisdom (Prov. 30:3). Our verse is to be understood as follows: and that He be not wroth with all the congregation, for you will atone for them.
[BUT LET YOUR BRETHREN, THE WHOLE HOUSE OF ISRAEL.] You will find the meaning of this alluded to in the Torah portion Behold, I Set (Deut. 11:26).

AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO AARON. For Aaron was a prophet. Others say through Moses, as in And the Lord spoke again unto Ahaz (Is. 7:10). God cautioned Aaron and his sons to keep the law so that they do not die as Aaron’s oldest sons died.

NOR STRONG DRINK. Made from any kind of wheat, honey, or dates, for wine destroys the reason of the one who imbibes it and he confuses things. Hence Scripture states, And that ye may put difference (v. 10). Since you are a kohen gadol you will differentiate between a holy place and a common place. The word chol (common) is related to the word chillul (profaned). It is possible that between the holy and the common means between a holy day and a common day.

AND BETWEEN THE UNCLEAN AND THE CLEAN. Among cattle and things that swarm in the water and that fly. Therefore the section opening with the words These are the living things (Lev. 10:11), and then the sections dealing with the woman who gives birth (Lev. 12:1-8) and the leprosy that is found in humans (Lev. 13:1-46), on garments (Lev. 13:47-59) and in houses (Lev. 14:33-53); one who experiences a seminal emission (Lev. 15:16-18); a male or female who experiences a flux (Lev. 15:1-15, 25-33); and a menstruant (Lev. 15:19-24) follow this section. This is the meaning of and between the unclean and the clean .
AND THAT YE MAY TEACH THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The rest of the commandments. Similarly and do according to all that the priests…shall teach you (Deut. 24:8).

TAKE THE MEAL-OFFERING. No one aside from those who are holy are fit to eat that which remains from the meal offering after part of it has been burned in honor of God. You shall begin to eat the portion which God has given you, to always take of God’s fire-offerings; this means all meal offerings, part of which was burned in honor of God.

[IN A CLEAN PLACE.] Even though it is outside the courtyard. The breast and the thigh shall be eaten by males and females, for Scripture clearly states, every one that is clean in thy house may eat thereof (Num. 18:11). Similarly slaves bought by money and born in the house, and a widow who returned to her father’s house. As you now eat the breast and the thigh, so shall the law be that you take these portions from all the sacrifices of peace offerings.
WAS BURNT. Soraf (was burnt) is a pu’al . Compare, morak (sodden) in it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water (Lev. 6:21).

IN THE PLACE OF THE SANCTUARY. At the opening of the tent of meeting, for this is clearly stated in Scripture. And He hath given it you [to bear the iniquity of the congregation ], for when you eat the sin offering God will bear the iniquity of the congregation. Or its meaning is, you will bear the iniquity of the congregation; that is, the sins of the congregation will be forgiven through you. Hence Scripture states, to make atonement .

BEHOLD, THE BLOOD OF IT WAS NOT BROUGHT INTO THE SANCTUARY WITHIN. Like the bullock brought by the kohen and the congregation for violation of any of the commandments. Should one ask, “Look, the bullock of the sin offering was burned and its blood was not brought into the inner sanctuary, the reference being to the place of the curtain and the golden altar?” Know that the sin offering bullock was to purify the altar, the he-goat sin offering was to atone for the people, and the flesh of the sin offering was for the kohen .
YE SHOULD CERTAINLY HAVE EATEN IT. Akhol tokhelu is to be rendered, ye should have certainly eaten it.

There are grammarians who say that the interrogative heh is not followed by a dagesh when the letter is vocalized with one of the seven “kings.” The letter following an interrogative heh is found with a dagesh only when it has a mobile sheva beneath it. The heh is vocalized with a pattach because two mobile shevas cannot come back to back. Now, since they found that the yod of ha-yitav (would it have been well pleasing) has a dagesh in it, they said that the heh of ha-yitav is the heh which indicates the direct object, like the heh of ha-shavah (that came) in that came back with Naomi (Ruth 2:6); the heh in ha-nimtze’u foh (that are found here) (I Chron. 29:17); the heh in ha-hullalah (the renowned) in The renowned city (Ezek. 26:17). These hehs are in place of the word asher (that). This is the meaning of ha-yitav (would it have been well pleasing). They further said that ve-akhalti (and if I had eaten) is a verb in the perfect. If the word were an imperfect it would have been ultimately accented like the words vedibbarti (I have also spoken) in I have also spoken unto the prophets (Hosea 12:11) and ve-dibbarti (and I will speak) in And I will speak with thee (Ex. 25:22). The meaning of the first half of our verse is, my sons who were burned today offered their sin offering and their burnt offering, for the bull-calf and the ram were offered on behalf of Aaron and his sons.

AND THERE HAVE BEFALLEN ME SUCH THINGS AS THESE. The reference is to troubles or anxiety because of the death of the sons. It was because of this that I was not able to eat the entire sin offering, but I ate enough of it to find favor in the eyes of God, that is, an amount which is enough to fulfill my obligation. However, in the opinion of the transmitters of tradition the heh of ha-yitav is an interrogative heh and the word is irregular. It is also irregular according to the explanation which I mentioned above, for we do not find in all of Scripture the definite article heh prefixed to a verb in the imperfect. The meaning of ve-akhalti chattat is to be interpreted as, and if I had eaten the sin offering. We also find words in the imperfect that are penultimately accented. Compare, ve-ganavti (and steal) in lest I be poor, and steal (Prov. 30:9). The meaning of our clause is, I was mourning, and a mourner does not eat of the sin offering. Its meaning is similar to I have not eaten thereof in my mourning (Deut. 26:14).
AND THE LORD SPOKE UNTO MOSES AND TO AARON. For Aaron is the kohen who teaches and who differentiates between the unclean and the clean.
PARTETH. Mafreset (parteth) is an adjective. Similarly makrin mafris (horned and hoofed) (Ps. 69:32). It means all animals which are described as having a hoof.
AND IS WHOLLY CLOVEN-FOOTED. Shosa’at (wholly cloven) is an adjective. The meaning of ve-shosa’at shesa perasot (and is wholly cloven-footed) is, whose hoofs are cloven.

AND CHEWETH THE CUD. Gerah (cud) is related to the word garon (throat). The word ma’alat (cheweth) is a verb in the present. Scripture mentions the camel (v. 4), the rockbadger (v. 5), the hare (v. 6), and the swine (v. 7) because each one has one sign. It is the style of Scripture to mention the male of each species because the masculine also takes in the feminine. Scripture mentions the arnevet (hare). Some say that it does so because the male is not found among them. There are others who say that the male turns into a female and vice versa. However, the first interpretation appeals to me.

AND THEIR CARCASSES YE SHALL NOT TOUCH. Scripture does not mention that one who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening. However, we know this from tradition. Now, the one who deliberately touches their carcass incurs the penalty of flogging, for he violated a negative commandment.

[9. IN THE SEAS.] If we pursue the literal meaning of the verse without the tradition of the rabbis, then the fish that are found in the lakes ( agammim ) are prohibited, for Scripture specifies the seas and the rivers .
FINS AND SCALES. Snappir ve-kaskeset (fins and scales) is to be rendered as the Aramaic translator does.

OF ALL THAT SWARM IN THE WATERS. They are the small creatures that were created from the water. The waters contain living creatures that are both male and female. After stating they are a detestable thing unto you Scripture goes on to say, and they shall be a detestable thing unto you (v. 11) in order to explain in what way they shall be detestable namely, ye shall not eat of their flesh ( Ibid .). Note, fish are called flesh. However, what the sages of blessed memory said with regard to vows refers to the custom of their generations. Scripture adds, Whatsoever hath no fins nor scales to include all waters, for Scripture earlier mentioned only the seas and the rivers.

THE GREAT VULTURE The meaning of nesher (the great vulture) is known. This is also the bird which has the same name in the language of the Ishmaelites. There is something of a proof that this is the case, because the two languages are related.

AND THE OSPRAY. Even though there is an individual opinion that it (the osprey) is not found in inhabited places, the Gaon erred in rendering it al enka , for this term in the language of the Ishmaelites refers to something that never existed. It refers to something that was not created and never was. It is only employed metaphorically. The Arab grammarians admit this. This being the case, it is not possible that the Torah would prohibit something that never existed.

AND THE KITE. The term da’ah (kite) is a general term which takes in two kinds, namely, the da’ah (kite) and the dayyah (falcon). Compare, tzippor (birds), the word used for a turtle-dove and a young pigeon in but the birds divided he not (Gen. 15:10). Now the transmitters of tradition who said that the ra’ah (glede) is to be identified with the da’ah (kite) are correct. The argument of Rabbi Jonah, who asked how is it possible to say be on guard because of the aryeh (lion) and the layyish (lion), is turned aside. Others say that nesher (the great vulture) is connected to the word ashurennu (I see him) (Num. 23:9); peres (bearded vulture) is related to the word pros (deal) in Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry (Is. 58:7); ozniyyah (osprey) is related to the word oz (mighty) and its nun is superfluous. It is the bird which is called akba ; da’ah (kite) is related to the word yideh (swoopeth) in as the vulture swoopeth down (Deut. 28:49); ayyah (falcon) is so called because it is accustomed to dwell in certain well-known islands ( iyyim );
orev (raven) is related to the word erev (evening). It is so called because of its darkness.

AND THE OSTRICH. Some say that the bat ha-ya’anah (ostrich) is a kind among whom males are not found. It is like the hare. There is no argument from the word ka-ye’enim (like the ostriches) (Lam. 4:3), for the reference is to females as in the case of ye’elim (wild goats) (Ps. 104:18) and rechelim (ewes) (Gen. 32:15).
AND THE NIGHT-HAWK. Tachmas (night-hawk) is related to the word chamas (violence) (Gen. 5:11).
THE SEA-MEW. The shachaf (sea-mew) gives birth to consumption ( shachefet ) (Lev. 26:16).
AND THE HAWK. The netz (hawk) has many feathers. It most likely refers to the well-known bird which always spreads its wings to the south, for it seeks a warm place.

AND THE LITTLE OWL. The word kos (little owl) is similar to the word kos (owl) in as an owl of the waste places (Ps. 102:7). Some say that the bird is hidden ( nikhseh ) from the eyes of people. It therefore rests in uninhabited places.
AND THE CORMORANT. Some say that the shalakh (cormorant) is so called because its nature is to cast ( le-haslikh ) its offspring down.
AND THE GREAT OWL. The yanshuf (great owl) is a bird that flies at night ( neshef ), for it cannot see during the day because of the brightness of the sun light.
AND THE HORNED OWL. Whoever looks at the tinshemet (the horned owl) is astonished ( yishom ). The term tinshemet is also found among the swarming things (v. 30).
AND THE PELICAN. Some say that the ka’at (pelican) is a bird whose nature is to regurgitate ( le-haki ) its food.

AND THE CARRION-VULTURE. The Gaon says that the racham (carrion-vulture) is the animal which is similarly called in Arabic, with the chet interchanging with a khaf , for they are written with the same letter. Others say that racham refers to a bird that has pity ( merachem ) upon its offspring.
AND THE STORK. Some say the chasidah (stork) is the bird which appears at certain well-known times in the year. Others say that it scatters loving kindness ( chesed ). This is far-fetched.
AND THE HERON. The anafah (heron) grows angry ( yitannef ) quickly.
AND THE HOOPOE. The Sadducees say that the dukhifat (hoopoe) refers to the chicken. However, they are the world’s greatest fools, for who told them this?
AND THE BAT. A small bird that flies at night. The word atalef (bat) is a quadriliteral; that is, it comes from a four-letter root.

Note that the word teshakketzu in teshakketzu min ha-of (these ye shall have in detestation among the fowls) (v. 13) has a slightly different grammatical meaning from teshakketzu in al teshakketzu et nafshotekhem (ye shall not make yourselves detestable) (v. 43). In the latter instance the word nafshotekhem (yourselves) is the object, while in the case of the fowl (v. 13) its meaning is, you shall know that they are detestable and they shall be considered detestable to you. All winged swarming things that at times fly and at times go upon all fours are detestable.
WHICH HAVE JOINTED LEGS. The main reading is the one that spells lo with a vav .

TO LEAP. The word le-natter has no brother. The Aramaic translator renders le-natter ba-hen by le-kappatza behen; since the word le-kappatza is similar to mekappetz (leaping) (Cant. 2:8), its meaning is leaping. He translated correctly.
[THE LOCUST.] The word arbeh (locust) is connected to the word ribbuy (large amount).
AND THE BALD LOCUST. The sale’am (bald locust) refers to a kind of locust which climbs on rocks ( sela’im ).

AND THE CRICKET. If the word chargol (cricket) is a quadriliteral, then it has no brother. If it is a combination of two words like the word palmoni (certain one) in unto that certain one who spoke (Dan 8:13), then the nature of the chargal is the reverse of the nature of the sale’am (bald locust).
AND THE GRASSHOPPER. Its meaning is known from the language of the Ishmaelite.

[BUT ALL WINGED SWARMING THINGS.] Scripture had previously stated, that go upon all fours (v. 20). The Torah now states, But all winged swarming things, which have four feet , because it is possible that there is a swarming creature that has four legs but that does not walk upon them but only flies.

AND BY THESE YE SHALL BECOME UNCLEAN. By all winged swarming things that have four feet; And these ye shall have in detestation among the fowls . Others believe that the word elleh (these) (v. 24) refers to among all the beasts and to And whatsoever goeth upon its paws (v. 27). I believe that the word elleh refers to all those mentioned above.

YE SHALL BECOME UNCLEAN. The word tittamma’u (ye shall become unclean) is a hitpa’el . The tet receives a dagesh because the tav is swallowed. The same is the case with the word middabber (speaking) in then he heard the Voice speaking unto him (Num. 7:89) and the word mittaher (cleansed) in And he that is to be cleansed shall wash (Lev. 14:8).
SHALL BE UNCLEAN UNTIL THE EVEN. Scripture chose the path of brevity, for the unclean must bathe in water.

AND WHOSOEVER BEARETH. Bearing is more serious than touching. Therefore the bearer must wash his garments. How much more so [must he bathe] his body. The same law applies to all beasts. Scripture also follows the path of brevity here. The verse is to be understood as follows, or is clovenfooted but cheweth not the cud or cheweth the cud but is not cloven-footed. Scripture has previously stated, and their carcasses ye shall not touch; they are unclean unto you (v. 8).

[EVERY ONE THAT TOUCHETH THEM.] This means everyone who touches any of the above-mentioned carcasses shall become unclean until the evening, for that is the law regarding the previously mentioned carcasses. There is a type of misbeliever who belongs to the Sadducee heresy who says that every one that toucheth them means whoever touches them while they are alive shall be unclean. There is no need to respond to insane talk, for Scripture only prohibited their flesh. It states, and their carcasses ye shall not touch (v. 8).

AND WHATSOEVER GOETH UPON ITS PAWS. At first the law is the same. Similarly And he that beareth the carcass of them (v. 28). This verse affirms my explanation of the words And by these ye shall be come unclean (v. 24), for Scripture there states, And whosoever beareth aught of the carcass of them (v. 25). Both of them are in one section.
The reason Scripture states, They are unclean unto you , is that it wants to include all of Israel: men, women, and children. One law applies to all.

AND THESE ARE THEY WHICH ARE UNCLEAN UNTO YOU. By touch. We also are not able to actually know what these eight creatures refer to. This is also true of the fowl. We can only know their identity by tradition.
[THESE ARE THEY WHICH ARE UNCLEAN.] It means that these alone are the unclean which, when dead, defile you.
The meaning of shall be unclean until the even is, after he bathes he shall be unclean until the evening.
IT MUST BE PUT INTO WATER. The garment or the sack or the vessel which is susceptible of uncleanness. We have a need for tradition regarding these things.
WHEREIN TO ANY OF THEM FALLETH. Me-hem is to be rendered, any one of them. Compare, And was buried in the cities of Gilead (Jud. 12:7).
AND ALL DRINK. Mashkeh (drink) is a noun. Mashkeh in Now I was giving drink to the king (Neh. 1:11) is a verb in the present tense.
Now, an oven (v. 35) which is used to bake bread and a range ( Ibid .) which is used to cook meat shall be broken into pieces, for they are unclean. This is the decree of the king.

A CISTERN. The Hebrew word be’er (well) is a feminine. It bubbles forth. Compare, As a well (bir) welleth with her waters (Jer. 6:7). However, a bor (cistern) is dug or excavated to store the rain from the sky. If so, the well is a fountain. There is no need to mention rivers. Mikveh mayim (a gathering of water) is connected to bor (cistern), for there are borot (cisterns) without water. Some say that mikveh is missing a vav . Compare, Reuben, Simeon (Ex, 1:2), and shemesh yare’ach (the sun moon) (Hab. 3:11).
BUT HE WHO TOUCHETH THEIR CARCASS. The water that touches their carcasses will be unclean.
SOWING. Zeru’a (sowing) is an adjective. It is similar to a pa’ul . On the other hand, there might be two nouns for the word seed. And gave them pulse (zeronim) (Dan. 1:16) is proof of this.

BUT IF WATER BE PUT. If they water their field and aught of their carcasses fall on the seed. Some say on the water. The word yuttan (be put), which is singular, governs mayim (water). We find a similarity in because the water (meh) of sprinkling was not dashed (zorak) against him (Num. 19:13). The word yuttan is similar to yukkach (be fetched) in Let now a little water be fetched (Gen. 18:4). It belongs to the heavy conjugation to which a letter is added.
OF WHICH YE MAY. Asher hi la-khem le-okhlah means of which ye may eat.
SHALL BE UNCLEAN UNTIL THE EVEN. After he bathes in water.
[AND HE THAT EATETH.] The law regarding he that eats is stricter. It is similar to the law governing he that that carries, for both bear. One carries outside and the other inside.
[AND EVERY SWARMING THING.] This means all swarming things of the earth. The eight swarming creatures are included. Scripture mentions that they are not to be eaten.
THE BELLY. The word gachon (belly) is similar to the word gechonekha (thy belly) in upon thy belly shalt thou go (Gen. 3:14).
AND WHATSOEVER GOETH UPON ALL FOURS. Among the swarming things which are small, as I explained with regard to the swarming things in the water.
MANY FEET. The word marbeh (many) is an adjective. It is in the construct.
YE SHALL NOT MAKE YOURSELVES DETESTABLE. By being filthy and dirty.
NEITHER SHALL YE MAKE YOURSELVES UNCLEAN. For it is known that that which is eaten turns into the flesh of the one who ingests it.

THAT YE SHOULD BE DEFILED THEREBY. The word ve-nitmetem (that ye should be defiled) is missing an alef . Compare, reshit (beginning) in from the beginning of the year (Deut. 11:12). Others say that they come from two roots. The word nitminu (unclean) in And reputed unclean in your sight (Job 18:3) is proof. It means that you do not become dumb-witted.

YE SHALL THEREFORE BE HOLY, FOR I AM HOLY. Hence I told you neither shall ye defile yourselves (v. 44). The vav is similar to the unaspirated fah in Arabic. Similarly the vav in va-ya’azov (left) in left his servants (Ex. 9:21). There are many such instances.

[FOR I AM THE LORD.] This means I did not take you out of Egypt for any reason but to be your God. If you will not be holy, I will not be a God to you. Hence if you want Me to be your God you must be holy.
TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE UNCLEAN. Among the fowl and that which swarms in the water.
THAT MAY BE EATEN. That is permitted to be eaten.
THAT MAY NOT BE EATEN. According to the words of the Torah.

IF A WOMAN BE DELIVERED. After Scripture concludes the law of clean and unclean food, it deals with human uncleanliness. The Torah starts with the woman who gives birth, because human life begins at birth. Many say that if the woman produces the seed first, then she gives birth to a male. Scripture therefore states, and bear a man-child . The wise men of the Greeks similarly believed that the seed is of the woman. The seed of the male congeals. All of the child is created out of the blood of the woman. Note, the meaning of tazri’a (be delivered) means will give seed, for a woman is like the ground.

The vav of ve-tame’ah (then shall be unclean) is like the unaspirated vav in Arabic. The reason that she is unclean for seven days is that she must wait until she completes a quarter of days. We find a similarity in the days of illness, for a change is seen at the end of the seven days.
THE IMPURITY OF. The word niddat (impurity of) is a noun. It follows the paradigm of bizzat (spoil of). Both words come from a double root.
HER SICKNESS. Devotah (her sickness) is a noun in the plural. Compare, madveh (diseases) in the evil diseases of Egypt (Deut. 7:15). The blood that comes out is an illness in the woman’s body.

AND IN THE EIGHTH DAY. Our wise men, of blessed memory, said during the day, not at night. Now a child born a half hour before sunset is circumcised after six and half days, for the day of the Torah is not measured by twenty-four hours.

SHALL BE CIRCUMCISED. Yimmol (shall be circumcised) is a nifal . Compare, yikkon (be established) in shall not be established (Ps. 101:7). According to this opinion, yimmol is related to the word mullim (circumcised) in were circumcised (Josh. 5:5). It is also possible that yimmol is missing a nun and is related to the word u-nemaltem (and ye shall be circumcised) (Gen. 17:11). Yimmol is like the word yiddor (voweth) in When a man voweth a vow unto the Lord (Num. 30:3). Scripture omits the one who performs the circumcision, such as the father or the Beth Din (court).
HIS FORESKIN. It is known that the foreskin is on the private part. This is not the case regarding the foreskin of the heart, the lip, and the ear, for all of them are connected to another word.

[PURIFICATION.] The heh of tohorah (purification) is unsounded. It should have been pronounced. It is like the heh in lah (it) in and called it Nobah (Num. 32:43). The meaning of deme tohorah (the blood of purification) is clean blood. This blood, in contrast to dam niddah (menstrual blood), is clean. It does not cause uncleanliness. The forty days that God decreed regarding a male child corresponds to the time it takes for the form of the male to be completed in the womb. It takes double that time for a female. This is clear and tested.
SHE SHALL TOUCH NO HALLOWED THING. Such as the tithe, trumah , and the flesh of peace offerings.
NOR COME INTO THE SANCTUARY. The courtyard of the tent of meeting or into the temple courtyard.
Be-deme tohorah (in the blood of purification) (v. 4) and al deme tohorah (in the blood of purification) have one meaning.

OF THE FIRST YEAR. If we did not have tradition, who would explain whether ben shenato (of the first year) means exactly one year, or less than a year, or a year plus? Some say that the reason a woman who gives birth brings a lamb for a burnt offering is that she may have had some unseemly thought because of her pain when giving birth. She brings a sin offering because she might have uttered some unseemly thing with her lips.

AND HE SHALL OFFER IT. This one and the other one, the lamb and the turtle-dove or the young pigeon. Scripture employed an abridged style. It similarly does not mention the snipping of the head of the fowl brought for a sin offering, for the kohen does not eat of the sin offering fowl.
AND MAKE ATONEMENT FOR HER. As I explained.
AND SHE SHALL BE CLEANSED FROM THE FOUNTAIN OF HER BLOOD. This is a sign that she does not naturally became cleansed until the days that are enumerated arrive.
AND IF HER MEANS SUFFICE NOT. This means the same as but if his means suffice not (see Lev. 5:11).
AND THE PRIEST SHALL MAKE ATONEMENT FOR HER, AND SHE SHALL BE CLEAN. This teaches that if the kohen does not make atonement for her she shall not be clean. This applies only in the Land of Israel.
